quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
Blocks your side vision.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Has no labels or markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see clearly to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels showing the maker's name, instructions, and safety standards.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A dirt or gravel road
Oil in the center of a lane
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery: wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal plates. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
Near the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually this means the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors more than side mirrors, so this position increases visibility.

questions.question: When using an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat for comfort.
Assume it is in good condition.
Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride normally since all bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding, learn how it works. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to get familiar with them.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long denim pants
Athletic shoes

questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride with the headlight on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Make yourself easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing and riding with your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment:

options.text: Starts with the first drink.
Starts at half the legal limit.
Occurs only at the legal limit.
Occurs only after multiple drinks.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired below the legal alcohol limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: Penalties for drinking and riding are:

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not very harsh.
Optional.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, the passenger should:

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when the rider leans. The passenger should sit forward without crowding the rider and hold firmly onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn at night.
Not be worn during the day.
Never be worn.
Not be worn at night.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing to be more visible, especially at night. Bright colors with reflective materials help other drivers see you.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should take only a few minutes.

questions.question: The correct body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Allows you to sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Allows you to sit far back and stretch to reach the grips.
Makes you lean forward so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: Common drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually won't affect your ability to ride safely.
Have no risk to your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
Not let them ask questions.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to stay safe. Never assume your passenger knows what to do. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If the road is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing later than usual.
Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight that changes how your motorcycle handles. Expect slower acceleration and turning, and need more space to stop. Ride slowly, slow down sooner, increase your space cushion, and wait for larger traffic gaps.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should use your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must happen within posted speed limits and only in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Are usually minimal.
Often cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your riding ability. Some medications become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only when it is cool outside.
Only when it is warm outside.
Only if you will ride for more than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. This protects you in hot weather too. It helps protect your skin from the sun and prevents dehydration.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.explanation: To reduce injury, riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid a crash?

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep other drivers guessing about what you will do.
Always stay very close to other vehicles.
Ride on the road shoulder.

questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals and brake light. Position your motorcycle where others can see it. Keep space around your bike. Always look ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover the ankle
A snug-fitting baseball cap
Gloves

questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and pants, high boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. These items protect you from injury.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Clothes made from synthetic materials
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective gear to make yourself and your motorcycle easier to see. This helps other drivers spot you.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
Alcohol stays in your body forever.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body removes alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour at a slow rate.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A low tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: How can you prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Go faster.
Slow down.
Make sudden movements.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Sudden movements can make your motorcycle skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: One benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle is:

options.text: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks will take a lot of time.
Maintenance will cost a lot of money.
Maintenance checks can help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will keep running like new. Regular maintenance checks help keep your motorcycle in good condition.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces are hard to control on a motorcycle. Which one is a slippery surface?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: When buying a protective jacket or pants, look for:

options.text: Leather material.
Polyester material.
Light materials.
Dark colors.

questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, brake lights, and good lane position to show your plans. Keep safe distance, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to dangers.
So you can tailgate.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you room to stop or swerve if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards like potholes.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of the lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars form a greasy strip in the center of each lane. When dry, it is usually safe for motorcycles. Avoid it when wet.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Honk your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let tailgaters pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and create more danger.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Protects your eyes and face.
Is not recommended.
Is required.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. A windshield on your motorcycle may mean you don't need eye protection by law, but a face shield is still a good idea.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms supporting your body rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance in turns. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Sit close enough that your arms bend slightly at the handgrips. Keep your feet on the footrests.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out and hit you.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for parking.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out and hit you.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous because a driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your path. Pedestrians may step out between cars.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, what should you do?

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. You should check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle tire grip best?

options.text: Dry pavement
Gravel
Snow
Leaves

questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after a crash?

options.text: Look it over carefully.
Replace it.
Give it to another rider.
Put on a new chin strap.

questions.explanation: Always replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
A jacket that covers your arms, but no long pants.
Long pants that cover your legs, but no jacket.
Whatever feels most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover both your arms and legs completely for protection.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding in another vehicle's blind spot?

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you move out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: When you see a bump or pothole ahead, why should you rise off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you.
So you can see the bump better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off the seat lets your joints absorb some of the force. This keeps the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: How does carrying a passenger affect motorcycle riding?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for beginning riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It helps new riders learn different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.
